name: Polycarp of Smyrna
credit: Polycarp of Smyrna, Orthodox fresco (imagined likeness; no authentic portrait survives) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Polycarp was bishop of Smyrna in Asia Minor in the early second century. Later Christian writers, notably Irenaeus, say that in his youth he had known the apostle John and others who had seen the Lord, which made him a living link between the apostles and the next generation of the Church.

He was martyred at Smyrna, traditionally around AD 155 at a great age, as told in the Martyrdom of Polycarp, which is held in this archive under The Apostolic Fathers. His one surviving writing is a short letter to the church at Philippi, sent with the letters of Ignatius of Antioch that he had collected.
